A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Guided Diffusion Bridges. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial revisions and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of Brownian/OU bridges, cell differentiation, FitzHugh–Nagumo dynamics and stochastic landmark matching, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original simulations across the same model families, revised empirical analyses, and new training-time and parameter-count measurements.

M1.justification: The guided-proposal correction, variational loss and training algorithm remain fundamentally unchanged. Local components change: the cell auxiliary drift becomes 1−x instead of −x, cell/FHN networks use LipSwish instead of tanh, and the cell network changes from four to three hidden layers.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Brownian/OU bridges, normal/rare/multimodal cell conditioning, partially observed FHN conditioning, and ellipse landmark matching. Revised process parameters, network configurations and landmark dimensionality remain settings within these retained tasks.

E2.justification: The principal external baseline families remain unchanged. v3 Table 1 adds OU and landmark efficiency comparisons against Heng et al.'s score matching and Baker et al.'s adjoint forward method, absent from those comparisons in v1. Figure 14 also adds an uncorrected guided-proposal comparator alongside the neural bridge and pCN-corrected proposal.

E3.justification: Appendix B substantially revises reported experimental settings. Brownian training changes from 60,000 to 25,000 trajectories, batch size 20 to 50, and time step 0.005 to 0.002. Cell/FHN training budgets, architectures and pCN schedules change; linear histograms increase from 1,000 to 50,000 samples. The new timing comparison specifies equal gradient-step counts and batch sizes and uses 20-dimensional landmarks, distinct from the 100-dimensional illustration.

E4.justification: Linear sensitivity studies change from primarily drift-parameter sweeps to variations in drift, noise and OU mean, with revised error maps showing sampled regions. v1's two-chain cell mode-coverage diagnostic in Figure 12 is removed. v3 Figure 14 adds a comparison exposing raw guided-proposal failures and the effects of neural correction or pCN updates.

E5.justification: Appendix B.5 changes the reported landmark experiment from one pCN chain to four independent chains and explicitly averages acceptance over them. This revises replication reporting, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-training uncertainty. Histogram error bars represent distribution discrepancies, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds concrete cost results: Table 1 reports OU training times of 44.12 seconds for the neural bridge, 65.55 for score matching and 162.68 for adjoint forward. Rare-cell results change from catastrophic score-matching failure to approximately correct dynamics with excess dispersion. FHN findings change from incomplete mode recovery to both methods capturing bimodality. These results accompany revised settings and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the central KL identity and Appendix A.2 proof from L + log(tilde h/h) to L − log(tilde h/h). It replaces v1's claim that any local minimizer recovers the exact bridge with a condition requiring attainment of the analytic bound. It also formalizes boundedness and generalizes the OU derivation. However, the new OU correction in Equation (46) has a guiding-term sign inconsistent with Equations (27) and (44).

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions: variational neural correction of guided proposals, efficient independent sampling, conditional-sample training and robustness under difficult conditioning. Revised terminology and new computational measurements clarify or support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v1 states that sufficient absolute-continuity conditions hold for all examples; v3 Section 3.4 explicitly exempts FHN and instead invokes empirical support. v3 also qualifies neural accuracy outside well-sampled regions and adds a stochastic-flow explanation for landmark topology preservation. The detailed Monte Carlo/discretization explanation of loss fluctuations is removed, while the general mode-seeking limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B extensively revises network, optimizer, sampling, training-budget and MCMC details. v3 newly supplies parameter counts and training times, but removes v1's rare-FHN nonuniform-grid description and score-matching JAX-port/custom-embedding details. Algorithm 2 changes its documented recording step to save states after rejected proposals too. The reproducibility code link is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2019) for LipSwish, Sommer et al. (2021) for stochastic flows, and Domingo-Enrich et al. (2025) for adjoint matching. It removes the Liptser–Shiryaev, PyTorch and attention citations. The central positioning as guided proposals combined with variational learning remains unchanged; publication updates to existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The preliminaries, method exposition, experimental narratives and appendix instructions undergo extensive rewriting. v3 separates guided proposals into their own subsection, introduces labeled definitions and remarks, adds Section 5.5, and substantially rewrites the linear-process, FHN and landmark discussions.

P2.justification: Most experimental figures move from the main text to the appendix. Linear histograms and sensitivity panels are split and regrouped, error maps gain trajectory overlays, and a new cell overview appears. Landmark comparisons become a three-row display, the two-chain cell figure disappears, and a computational comparison table is added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the central justification by correcting the KL sign and overstrong local-minimizer claim, explicitly qualifying the FHN guarantee, and adding computational evidence for efficiency. These gains are tempered by the newly inconsistent OU correction in Equation (46), limited timing-protocol disclosure, and removal of the two-chain diagnostic. The net improvement is supported but limited; revised experimental settings prevent treating the changed plots as controlled performance gains.
